chunks: Surely those who had gone before them had also plotted; but God's is all the planning, for He has knowledge of what each does. The unbelievers will soon learn for whom is the guerdon of Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's plan versus human plotting?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from the temporary 'plotting' (makr) of the disbelievers to the ultimate 'divine scheme' (lillahi al-makr) that secures victory for the faithful, echoing the strategy of Imam Ali at Khaybar. It underscores God's omniscience over individual deeds as a precursor to the final reckoning, assuring that the 'good end' (uqba al-dar) belongs to the God-fearing, a concept central to the expectation of the Mahdi's triumph over oppression.
